newsitem.title: GERMANY: German institute sees slack consumer demand.
newsitem.headline: German institute sees slack consumer demand.

text.p: A leading German economic research institute said on Wednesday it did not see any immediate recovery in consumer demand.
The DIW think tank said in its latest report it did not expect the relatively strong consumer spending in the first half of the year to continue.

A rise in social security contributions would hit net incomes in the second half and this would be compounded in 1997 by the government's austerity package which would take more purchasing power out of the economy as would a rise in pension contributions, it said.

The DIW said most households expected their financial situation to worsen in the months ahead and would thus refrain from large purchases. This picture matched the poor mood of the retail sector, it said.
